description: Additive encounters tied to real POIs from locations.json. These trigger on first visit, repeat visits, or special conditions.

encounters.dialog: Captain Rex squints at you from the shadow of the concrete wall. "Another stray. Hope you bite raiders and not my people."
Your Pip-Boy crackles. A burst of static forms a pattern — almost like coordinates.
Your Geiger counter screams to life. For a moment, you swear the clicks form words.
The air hums. The ground vibrates. Something beneath the soil is awake.
A radstorm rolls across the horizon, shifting unnaturally as if avoiding you.
The storm whispers. Not wind. Not static. Something else.
A deep, resonant roar echoes from the cavern. Something massive is moving inside.
Fresh claw marks line the rock. Whatever lives here is hunting.
A shadow crosses the ridge — too large, too fast. You are not alone.
The rocks shift. Something is stalking you from above.
The sand crunches like glass beneath your boots. A faint green glow pulses in the crater.
Your Pip-Boy picks up a faint signal — rhythmic, deliberate, almost like Morse code.
A long-dead alarm system flickers to life as you enter. Something in the lab recognizes you.
A terminal hums softly. The screen flashes: "CORE TEMPERATURE: RISING".
The wind carries a metallic taste. A distant echo bounces through the empty buildings.
A figure stands in a window for a moment — then vanishes when you blink.
Your Pip-Boy flashes a radiation warning so intense it nearly overloads the screen.
A deep rumble shakes the ground. Something beneath the reactor is still alive.
A distorted broadcast cuts through your radio: "HELLO, WASTELANDERS!"
The static forms a voice — faint, broken, familiar. Jax?
A scrap of paper sits on the bar: "DON'T TOUCH THE HUMMING CRATE — SPARKPLUG".
A drunk mutters about a hidden stash under the floorboards — might be worth a look.
Smoke rises from behind the building. Something was burned recently.
The ashes reveal a melted pre-war lockbox. Could be loot inside.
A merchant whispers: "Someone’s buying up pre-war tech. Paying in caps and silence."
The merchant offers a deal: a rare Pip-Boy mod for 200 CAPS.
A woman sweeps the porch of a ruined farmhouse. The gesture is too practiced. She's been doing it, you realize, for longer than anyone should.
She's still sweeping. The same three boards. The same practiced arc. She smiles when she sees you — warmly, perfectly — and you feel the wrongness of it like a stone in your boot.

A figure stands at the base of the relay tower — tall, dark-coated, watching you approach with the patience of someone who has done this many times before. "You're not the first person she's sent to find this place," he says. "You will be the last."

Near the tower's external access panel, half-buried in dust: a small neural chip. The serial number on it reads DLRS-7. There's something etched below it, in careful scratch-marks: LOOP CYCLE: 4,218,332.

Something feels wrong at the ridge line — a faint, subsonic hum from the direction of the tower. Your Pip-Boy stutters. For a moment, you thought you saw a woman standing here. Looking north. She wasn't there when you turned.

A settler at the well gestures toward the southern hills. "Saw him again last night. White jumpsuit. Sequins catching the moonlight. Just standing there on the ridge, real quiet." She pauses. "I know how it sounds. But it wasn't a ghoul. Ghouls don't have sideburns like that."
A handwritten note is pinned to the dino's tail: "KING SIGHTING - 3 NIGHTS IN A ROW - SOUTHEAST RIDGE - HE WAVED - I WAVED BACK - SIGNED, DEFINITELY NOT CRAZY"

The busker on the corner is playing something old and slow on a battered guitar. He stops when you approach. "You seen the King around? Not the Kings. The King. White suit. Black hair. Voice like warm gravel and whiskey." He looks south. "He comes through sometimes. Listens for a while. Tips better than anyone."

A securitron pauses its patrol at the Strip gate and swivels toward you. "Query: Have you observed an individual approximately 1.9 meters tall, white sequined suit, hair product above regulatory quantity?" It waits. "No reason. He is simply on the watch list. Positive watch list. Mr. House's request."

Scrawled on a concrete blast wall in blue paint: 'THE KING LIVES' with a crude silhouette of a man mid-hip-swivel. Below it, someone has added in careful handwriting: 'Confirmed. Boulder City. 0300 hours. He sang one song and walked west.' Below that, a third hand: 'He's real. I swear it.'

A dusty terminal in the control room shows an old personnel file: CAIN, T. - VAULT-TEC SYSTEMS ARCHITECT - STATUS: RESIGNED - NOTE: 'The experiment parameters are ethically problematic and I refuse to continue. I'm building something better.' The resignation date is 2073. The file was never archived.

Behind a broken panel in the Lucky 38's penthouse archive, you find a framed design sketch — hand-drawn, pre-war — labeled 'WASTELAND AESTHETIC PROPOSAL v.1' by 'L. BOYARSKY, ART DIRECTION'. It depicts a man in a Pip-Boy watching a nuclear mushroom cloud. The expression on the man's face is complicated. The sketch is beautiful.

Folded inside a dead scientist's notebook: a handwritten letter signed 'C. Avellone, Narrative Division, Vault-Tec.' It reads: 'If someone reads this after everything ends — the story was always about the people. Not the bombs. Not the vaults. Not the factions. The people make the story. I hope someone out there is still telling them.'

A pre-war holotape in a rusted broadcaster's booth, labeled 'FEARGUS URQUHART - VAULT-TEC EXECUTIVE MEMO, 2075'. The playback is partially corrupted, but audible: '...the vaults are not just shelters. They are a canvas. If we do this right, whatever comes out of them in a hundred years will be something new. Something... interesting. I'm genuinely excited to see what happens.' Static. End of recording.

Half-buried under irradiated rubble, a commemorative plaque: 'WASTELAND DEVELOPMENT PROJECT — LEAD DESIGNER: C. TAYLOR — THIS INSTALLATION REPRESENTS THE FIRST ATTEMPT TO MODEL POST-NUCLEAR HUMAN ADAPTATION UNDER CONTROLLED CONDITIONS. WE BELIEVE IN THE RESILIENCE OF THE HUMAN SPIRIT.' The irony of the location is not lost on you.

A figure stands at the crest of the road ahead — enormous, fur-clad, carrying what appears to be a repurposed pre-war fire axe. He raises it in greeting, or possibly challenge. It's a fine line with this one.
A man in tattered robes sits on an overturned crate beside the market, distributing something from a pack. He notices you. 'Water and stimpaks, no charge. Sit if you need to.' He means it.

An unmistakably blue cabinet stands beside the trading post — battered, pre-war, painted in a shade that doesn't quite match anything else in the Mojave palette. A brass plate on the door reads: POLICE PUBLIC CALL BOX. The door is ajar. From inside comes the sound of someone making tea.

A figure rises from the sand where no person should have been — silent, unannounced, perfectly still. He watches you with patience that reads as either calm or threat. Then: 'You are loud. Come. There is shade.' He disappears back into a depression in the rock as naturally as water drains.

An ancient ghoul sits on a rock at the ridge, looking west. His glow is faint — so long-lived that even the radiation seems accustomed to him. He doesn't turn when you approach. 'I was watching the same view,' he says, 'in a place that doesn't exist anymore. Different sky. Same quiet. Same feeling that it won't last.'
